provenance.observed_pattern: A DELETE statement filters rows using a subquery-backed NOT IN predicate and returns columns from each deleted row.
provenance.mysql_mariadb_translation: Translate the portable subquery predicate to MariaDB DELETE ... RETURNING using independently authored archive-index and archive-entry tables, with one orphan row returned and the remaining rows verified afterward.

fixture_notes: Two archive entries have indexed archive IDs and one orphan entry has an absent index; only the orphan is deleted and returned.
determinism_notes: Primary-key predicates and final-state ordering are fixed. The delete selects one orphan row, so the RETURNING result is deterministic.
setup: CREATE TABLE archive_index (archive_id INT PRIMARY KEY, archive_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE archive_entries (entry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, archive_id INT NOT NULL, entry_label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, bytes_used INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: DELETE FROM archive_entries WHERE archive_id NOT IN (SELECT archive_id FROM archive_index) RETURNING entry_id, archive_id, entry_label, bytes_used
SELECT entry_id, archive_id, entry_label, bytes_used FROM archive_entries ORDER BY entry_id

checks.sql: SELECT entry_id, archive_id, entry_label, bytes_used FROM archive_entries ORDER BY entry_id
